chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man hired a worker to build for him or do other work, and began giving him food, cotton, and other things. Then the price of the food and cotton changed from the price at which he gave it, either decreasing or increasing. Should he account for him at the price of the day he gave it, or at the price of the day of accounting? So he (peace be upon him) signed: He should account for him at the price of the day he stipulated to him, if God wills.

And he (peace be upon him) answered regarding the money that becomes due to the man, so he is given food with it at its due time, and he is not cut off (from service). Then the price changes. So he (peace be upon him) signed: For him is the price of the day he was given the food.
ai.seo_question: How should wages paid in goods be calculated if market prices change before final settlement?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'sighr al-yawm' (price of the day) in wage contracts paid in kind, ensuring that fluctuations in market value do not unjustly enrich the employer or burden the worker. It establishes that the valuation is fixed at the time of the initial stipulation or delivery, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the real value of labor and preventing hidden usury (riba) through price volatility.
